title: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis
title_zh: 动物-藻类共生中远程肌动蛋白驱动的内共生体移动
abstract: In animal-microbe symbioses, established symbionts are often thought to be confined to a niche and to lose motile appendages such as flagella. Whether this loss implies immobility within the host remains poorly understood. We report long-range, host-driven symbiont mobility in a dinoflagellate-acoel worm symbiosis. Using long-term tracking, fluorescence, and electron microscopy, we find that hundreds of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10-20 μm in size) travel across the body of an acoel worm host (Waminoa sp.) at around 1 μm/s while confined inside a network of ultra-thin (∼200 nm) host parenchymal cells. We show this mobility is driven by host actin machinery, with symbionts moving faster than comparable actin-based transport systems despite confinement. We further show spatiotemporal regulation of symbiont distribution during diel rhythms and regeneration. By characterizing an active, host-cytoskeleton-driven mechanism of symbiont transport, our work expands our understanding of the regulatory strategies by which holobionts maintain dynamic homeostasis.
abstract_zh: 在动物-微生物共生中，已建立的共生体常被认为局限于特定生态位，并失去如鞭毛等运动附属物。是否失去运动性意味着在宿主体内不具移动性仍不清楚。我们报告了在甲藻-无腔虫共生中，宿主驱动的共生体远程移动。通过长期追踪、荧光和电子显微镜，我们发现数百个甲藻共生体（Amphidinium sp.，尺寸10-20 µm）在无腔虫宿主（Waminoa sp.）体内以约1 µm/s的速度穿越，且被限制在超薄（约200 nm）宿主实质细胞网络内。我们证明这种移动由宿主肌动蛋白机制驱动，且共生体移动速度超过同类肌动蛋白介导的运输系统，尽管受到限制。进一步，我们展示了共生体分布在昼夜节律和再生过程中的时空调控。通过表征一种主动的、由宿主细胞骨架驱动的共生体运输机制，我们的工作扩展了对全生物体维持动态稳态的调控策略的理解。
